about: The base rig's drivers (tools/body/rig_drive.py has each law), v2. Copied into rig.json at build ('girdle', 'helpers'). Run order: girdle, then the helpers in list order (unroll, twists, shares, points, aims). Upper-arm chain counter_twist amounts are 0.5 (1 - t) at the chain's weight nodes t = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 (weights.py RULES): half undone at the shoulder, none at the elbow; the thigh's 0.7 (1 - t) at t = 0, 0.5.

girdle.why: Scapulohumeral rhythm, the clavicle and the scapula driven from the humerus (rig_drive.girdle): tables of the arm's elevation A (deg from the torso's down axis), monotone C1 cubics flat past the ends, each relative to its value at the rest (MakeHuman's A-pose, A0 ~43 deg; the rest exactly neutral). Clavicle elevation and retraction: Ludewig, Phadke, Braman et al. 2009 (JBJS 91-A, 3D motion of the shoulder complex in 12 subjects: clavicle elevation ~10-15 deg, retraction ~15-30 deg, scapular upward rotation ~40-50 deg, posterior tilt ~20-30 deg over full elevation) and Inman, Saunders and Abbott 1944 (the setting phase: through the first ~30 deg the girdle barely moves, so the curves are nearly flat from 0 (hanging) to A0 and a hanging arm moves the clavicle and blade only a little down from rest). Protraction with forward reach (10 deg per unit of the arm's direction . front beyond rest) and the blade's forward glide (15 mm per unit) as the arm flexes forward (Ludewig 2009: scapular protraction in flexion). The upper arm keeps its world turn (the clip's aim).

retract_plane.why: P1 R2 law2: retraction by plane. The clavicle's retraction table (relative to the rest) is scaled by the arm's forward reach beyond the rest (d . front - d0 . front: 0 in abduction, full table; 0.4 of it from reach 0.4: the check's flexion 135 reads 0.39, its 90 0.64), faded in over elevation 95..120 deg: below it the full table (the hanging arm and the rest, where the plane is undefined, and flexion to 90: flex 90 outer outline 14.9 mm at 1.0, 20.5 at 0.35, 24.0 at 0). Flex 135 outer 14.1 mm at 1.0, 10.7 at 0, 4.9-6.2 at 0.25-0.5. Read by reach, not azimuth: the check's flexion from her A-pose sits at azimuth 35 (135) and 47 (90), the scapular plane, so the scapular plane at 135 (reach ~0.4) takes the flexion's scale too. Ludewig 2009: the clavicle and scapula sit protracted in high flexion against the retraction of abduction. Protraction by reach stays (protract_per_reach).

helpers.name: lowerarm_{s}
helpers.why: the ulna is a hinge: its roll goes to the hand

helpers.name: upperarm_share_{s}
helpers.why: P1 R2 law2: the share's hanging branch. amount 0.5 of the arm's turn beyond the clavicle when the arm is above the rest elevation (the cap turns with the humerus as it lifts); below.amount when it hangs below the rest (the deltoid's top stays under the acromion, riding the girdle), smoothstep-blended over the rest -+ band deg (no pop). Tuned by the arm_hang panel (top-drop ratio at 5 deg: 0.5 -> -0.54, 0.15 -> 0.04, 0 -> 0.54, -0.03 -> 0.84, -0.1 -> 0.99); the cost is the inner upper arm's known contact with the torso side 6-11 cm below the joint (1.9 -> ~9 mm deep at 5 deg).

helpers.name: delt_{s}
helpers.why: the deltoid bunches (wider across, shorter along) as the arm rises

helpers.name: pec_{s}
helpers.why: the front axillary fold follows the arm

helpers.name: lat_{s}
helpers.why: the back of the armpit follows the arm

helpers.name: glute_{s}
helpers.why: the glute's lower edge follows the thigh as it flexes (the fold rides with it)
